summary: The root دحر (daḥara) means to drive away, expel, or banish someone with roughness or violence. It implies pushing someone away, often with ignominy. This term is used to describe God expelling Satan.
lane: 1 دَحَرَهُ دحر دحره دحرة , (S, A, K,) aor. دَحَرَ , (K,) inf. n. دُحُورٌ (S, A, K) and دَحْرٌ , (T, K,) He (God, S) drove him away; expelled, or banished, him: he removed him; put, or placed, him at a distance, or away, or far away: (T, S, A, K:) he pushed, thrust, or repelled, him, (K,) with roughness, or violence, and ignominy. (TA.) It is said, in a form of prayer, اَلّٰهُمَّ ٱدْحَرْ عَنَّا الشَّيْطَانَ O God, drive away from us the devil. (TA.)
